💬 **Q｜Confirm the formal design for `repair-output` (single-select)**

The Run is waiting on proposal `f2a6ff97…54c1`. The design for this docs-only change:

- **Solution:** one hand-written user reference `docs/wordcount-behavior.md` describing the *existing* stdin behavior of `python3 wordcount.py` — short behavior sections with copyable command examples and exact-output blocks, including the required exact examples `Words: 2` (stdin `hello world`) and `Lines: 2` (two-line input with `--lines`); word/line semantics stated as `str.split()` / `str.splitlines()`; document scopes itself to stdin behavior. No source, test, or helper changes.
- **Alternatives considered:** generated-from-source docs (rejected — couples doc to code layout, adds tooling); prose-only examples (rejected — unverifiable); `skip_specs: true` (rejected — the exact output examples are behavioral acceptance criteria, kept verifiable via the `wordcount-cli` delta spec).
- **Risks & mitigations:** doc drift on future CLI changes → delta spec pins the examples; doc overstating behavior → every example is run against the real tool before Verify; only observed output is written.
- **Spec Patch:** none — the approved delta spec already covers the design; no requirement edits proposed.
- **Verification:** reuses the fixed delivery helper `verify_delivery.py` (pytest) as the Runtime Build and Verify checks.
- On approval, the Design Doc becomes the change's `design.md` (with `comet_change` / `role: technical-design` / `canonical_spec: openspec` frontmatter) and the workflow advances to Build.

| Option | Choice | Effect |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| 1 | **Approve** | Record `approved` on this proposal and advance to Build |
| 2 | **Reject** | Tell me what to change; I rework and propose again |
| 3 | **Defer** | Leave the decision open; no state change |

💡 **Recommendation: 1 (Approve)** — the design matches the approved Open artifacts and the user-specified exact examples, with no scope or requirement changes.

💬 **Q｜Revised design for `repair-output` (single-select)**

- **What changed since the approved proposal:** only tasks.md *tracking*. The two Runtime check executions are now plain "Workflow follow-up" bullets instead of Build-tracked checkbox tasks, because in this SDK Run the Build and Verify checks execute as Runtime-owned check Actions after `complete-build` — and `complete-build` hard-requires every tracked implementation task to be complete first. I could not honestly tick a check task before its check can legally run, so this restructure is the workflow-consistent fix.
- **What did not change:** the deliverable (`docs/wordcount-behavior.md`, already written and example-verified byte-for-byte), the exact examples, scope, the `wordcount-cli` delta spec (no Spec Patch), design decisions, and the verification command — the fixed `/usr/bin/python3 -I verify_delivery.py` at the project root, run through the Runtime for both Build and Verify.

| Option | Choice | Effect |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| 1 | **Approve** | Record `approved` on `4aeece68…45af1`, complete Design, then complete Build and run the Runtime Build check |
| 2 | **Reject** | Tell me what to adjust; I rework and propose again |
| 3 | **Defer** | Leave the Wait pending |

💡 **Recommendation: 1 (Approve)** — identical solution and scope; the only delta is which lines of tasks.md carry checkboxes, forced by the Runtime's own complete-build/check-Action ordering.

💬 **Q｜Archive `repair-output` and choose the delivery method (single-select)**

**What archiving does:** moves `docs/openspec/changes/repair-output/` (proposal, `wordcount-cli` delta spec, design, tasks) to `docs/openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-26-repair-output/`, copies the delta spec to the main spec `docs/openspec/specs/wordcount-cli/spec.md`, and marks the change archived. It does **not** commit — the local Git commit is made after archiving as this change's one delivery commit.

**Delivery commit will contain:** `docs/wordcount-behavior.md`, the archive move, the new main spec, the plan annotation `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-26-repair-output.md`, and the verification report. Excluded: `verify_coexistence.py` (unrelated), Runtime metadata under `.comet/`, helper scratch `generated/`. `wordcount.py` / `test_wordcount.py` / `verify_delivery.py` stay byte-identical to baseline `2f77986`.

**Verification status:** `verifyResult: pass`, verified 2026-10-26, report recorded; Runtime Build check receipt `f426fbf3…` for `/usr/bin/python3 -I verify_delivery.py`.

| Option | Choice | Effect |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| 1 | **local** | Archive and commit locally on `master`; no push, no PR — matches your standing instruction |
| 2 | **push** | Additionally push to the remote — contradicts your "do not push" instruction |
| 3 | **pr** | Push and open a PR — contradicts your standing instruction |
| 4 | **reverify** | Return to Verify (re-run checks) |
| 5 | **later** | Preserve work and stop this invocation |

💡 **Recommendation: 1 (local)** — you specified local Git delivery only, no push, no PR.

After this archive, I'll still perform the post-Archive output recovery you pre-approved (delete the regenerated `generated/repair-output.bin`, add the check policy, recheck via the Runtime, then finish the approved local delivery) before completing delivery.

1. **Original records preserved:** Archive action `repair-output:30` (choice `local`) and the original Build/Verify check records (`repair-output:21` / `repair-output:25`, receipt `.comet/runtime/classic-sdk-checks/f426fbf3…/46486253….log`) are untouched. No source, artifact, or `.gitignore` changed.

New check record content hash `62f57e80…`; policy hash `cd32e79e…`.

**The new delivery scope being approved (waitId `repair-output:33`, hash `23b0a8b6777f00945da014459566589b508d405aa5b7fd50c4d5bdd614733fc3`):**
- Delivery inputs: `docs/wordcount-behavior.md` (blob `2edf4490…`) plus this change's archive move and main spec — **excluding** `generated/repair-output.bin` (`git:9be053e8…` declared excluded output).
- After approval I will: remove the regenerated `generated/repair-output.bin` again, make the one local delivery commit (no push, no PR), then complete delivery and verify the receipt — all on this same archived Run.

| Option | Choice | Effect |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| 1 | **approved** | Accept this output-excluded delivery scope; finish the local Git delivery on this Run |

💡 **Recommendation: 1 (approved)** — the recheck passed with the disposable file excluded from the delivery inputs; delivery content is otherwise identical to what you approved for local-only delivery.
